title: International Mosquito Air and Ground Crew Memorial
memorial_details: The memorial consists of two main parts. The lower part is a plaque with the inscription, set on a small brick wall with brick pillars either side that reach the same height as the plaque, there are damaged sections of a Rolls Royce merlin engine either side of the paving. Above this there is a wall mounted replica Mosquito propeller with a small plaque beneath detailing its donation. This propeller replaces the previous aircrash damaged and twisted one which was stolen in 2005.
inscription: Main Plaque: (Royal Air Force Crest)/ International Mosquito Air and Ground Crew Memorial/ In memory of all Allied Mosquito Air and Ground Crews who serviced, flight tested and/ flew Mosquitos on worldwide operations during and after World War II./ Mosquitos were flown in a variety of roles, including bombing, pathfinding, unarmed photo/ reconnaissance, day and night intruders, night fighting, fighter/ground attack,/ courier operations, target towing and training./ The Mosquito was the most successful multi-role combat aircraft, engineered from wood and/ became known as the "Wooden Wonder". It was operated by two crew and was faster than most/ other allied or enemy aircraft of its time. The courage and dedication of both air and ground crew/ who flew and maintained the Mosquito was outstanding./ (Mosquito engraving)/ Sponsored by the Mosquito Aircrew Association/ Designed by R D S Coleman Constructed by I Rumney Propeller plaque: This Mosquito Propeller/ was kindly donated by/ Jackie & Colin Williams/ from/ Applied Fibreglass Ltd of Stowmarket
community_connection: The memorial is for Allied Mosquito Air and Ground Crews who served on worldwide operations during and after World War II. It was sponsored by the Mosquito Aircrew Association.
